findings.title: Login-cache invalidation can be skipped for IdPs linked to a disabled organization
findings.body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate compares getLoginPredicate() on the original and updated models, but the original model comes from getById() and is wrapped by createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(), whose isEnabled() also returns false when the linked organization (or organizations for the realm) is disabled. The JPA delegate used by getForLogin() nevertheless included that IdP in the cached ID set based on its stored enabled flag. Therefore, while the organization is disabled, changing a login-relevant field such as hideOnLogin, linkOnly, or enabled to make the IdP ineligible makes both predicates evaluate to false (or otherwise appear unchanged), so no login-cache invalidation is registered. The stale ID remains cached and, once the organization is re-enabled, getForLogin() can return an IdP that the uncached JPA query would no longer return to callers that do not re-check those flags.

findings.title: New test registers cleanup for a literal "alias" instead of the created IdPs
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin the cleanup is registered as testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove rather than using each created alias ("idp-alias-" + i, and similarly "idp-alias-20" at line 425). This attempts to remove a provider literally named "alias" and does not clean up the 21 providers created by the test, leaving them in the shared test realm to potentially affect other tests in the class and masking failures from the cleanup call itself.
